result:
I fixed F-DG1-132 and F-DG1-215 the way the assignment asked: by documenting the route as an accepted limitation, not by trying to block it. The lint still can't catch code that reaches `crypto.setEngine` by looping over the `node:crypto` exports without writing the name. A new test now records that this is deliberate. All required checks pass on Node 24.21.0.

**What changed (only the two permitted files):**
- **`apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts` (comments only, no logic change):** every comment that said `setEngine` (and rule 1 generally) is banned "in every form" now says "in every **spelled** form" and lists those forms. I also widened residual (a), using the assignment's wording, so it covers looking up exports of an allowed built-in like `node:crypto` (namespace or default import) by a key built at runtime. It names `crypto.setEngine` and gives two examples. It also says why a blanket ban isn't workable: `identity/routes.ts` and `access/rules.ts` use the same `new Map(Object.entries(x)).get(name)` pattern legitimately. Residuals (b) and (c) are unchanged.
- **`apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts`:** I fixed the same overclaim in the file header and above the S1–S3 tests. A new test checks that the four lookup forms E1–E4 produce no violations. Its comment says this is the accepted residual (a), not a missed violation, and that the forms should move into the violation table if a future lint closes the route. The S1–S3 spelled-name bans, the `node:crypto` positive control and the real module-tree check are untouched.

No migrations and no API endpoints. Nothing was committed.

**Checks run (offline, Node v24.21.0, pnpm 10.33.0):**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm vitest run apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts` | passed: 109 tests, including E1–E4, S1–S3, the positive control and the real module tree |
| `pnpm -r typecheck` | passed |
| `pnpm lint` | passed |
| `pnpm exec prettier --check` on the two files | passed |
| `pnpm test` | passed: 21 files, 302 tests |

**Gaps:**
- Nothing was run on Node 22, because there's no Node 22 install in this sandbox. The change is comments plus a lint assertion that doesn't depend on the Node version.
- `crypto.setEngine` is still reachable this way at runtime. That is exactly what the new test records.
- Other changes in the working tree aren't mine and I didn't touch them: `docs/delivery/findings.json` and `docs/delivery/decisions.md` (orchestrator) and `apps/web/**` (the parallel T-DG1-FE3 run). When this is committed, include only the two source files and the handback.

The handback, with the exact diff and the full test output, is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG1/round-11/T-DG1-BE12-backend-workflow-engineer.md`.
